item.title: LLM Inference Benchmarks
item.description:
Work in progress page…
LLM inference benchmarks I’ve done myself or collected from the community and other online resources.

A quick way to calculate your max theoritical output speed for a dense model is with bandwidth / size_of_llm_in_gb = max_tok_per_sec
For example, Llama 3.3 iQ5KM is 50 GB in size. A V100 16GB (SXM2) has 900GB/s of memory bandwidth. 900 / 50 = 18. Now of course, there is always going to be some overhead which is why my results are ~14 tokens per second which is about 80% of the theoritical max. As low as 70% will be commonplace. If you are getting less than 70% performance, try different quantization methods, inference backends, or operating systems. Typically, headless Linux (I prefer Ubuntu server) will get you better results than using Windows OS.

item.title: Directory Opus Review
item.description:
Made by GP Software 
Price: $89 AUD - Single License
Supports Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11, but not ARM.

I absolutely LOVE Directory Opus. As soon as I tried it for the first time, I knew I never wanted to go back to the mess that is Windows Explorer, and don’t even get me started on its buggier successor. I found DOpus when looking for an alternative to Windows Explorer that would allow me to scroll while dragging files; a very nice quality of life bonus to any file browser. At first, the high price point of $89 AUD (about $60 USD) put me off, but after running the trial, I knew it was the right choice. Really what amazes me the most, besides how polished it feels, is its INSANE amount of customization options available, including the ability to run scripts to customize functions.

item.title: Managing Your Digital Privacy
item.description:
Work in progress ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ {.is-info}

The “I have nothing to hide" argument annoys me so much because it shows that tech companies and the government have done such a good at convincing people that you only need privacy if you’re doing something malicious.

This is a HIGHLY recommended read: https://www.chronicle.com/article/why-privacy-matters-even-if-you-have-nothing-to-hide/

https://rejectconvenience.com/ - https://www.youtube.com/@rejectconvenience

If you want to start getting a better handle of your digital privacy, I recommend by first debloating your Windows 10 or 11 version by following my guide on /debloating-windows-os. This will block a lot of tracking telemetry microsoft includes which tracks nearly everything you do from searches in your start menu, opening steam, what games you play, what settings you open, etc. I’ll get a more detailed list of exactly what data microsoft collects on individuals and why people should care.

item.title: SERVERMAXXING
item.description:
AI Server Builds

Here are some server setups I’ll be covering that can run large models with budget prices. By budget I mean it won’t cost the same as a new Ferrari, which some SOTA systems can easily surpass. I’ll be going over specific hardware to look for in more detail over on the Server Building page. These aren’t branded products or off-the-shelf systems. I’ve curated these from community builds. I have personally built and tested multiple of these systems, while others are based on extensive research, real-world benchmarks, deep dives into component specs, and reports from users who’ve tried them out to give you an accurate picture of how they would work in a real-world situation.
You can find the all the benchmarks I’ve run myself and collected in the LLM Inference Benchmarks page.

Python

“Let me read you from the Zen of Python: There should be one and preferably only one obvious way to do it, which is why we have three different versions, 12 different ways to install them, and 80 different frameworks for the same thing: Easy Install, Anaconda, conda, pip, homebrew.” - Programmers Are Also Human

Uhhhh idk, this is for a bunch of stuff I’ve found so far that I haven’t found a place to categorize them into yet. Probably gonna be a place for all this stuff in the future as I add more to the site, but for now here it is

Minor annoyances and crap

I hate that little thing showing up on youtube thumbnails on my home page. It’s so easy to click on by accident if you’re opening a few pages in new tabs to queue up your watch list when you wanna waste time.
Here’s how I got rid of it:
Step 1: Get https://ublockorigin.com/ to block ads (https://adnauseam.io/ is a better option IMO because it poisons advertiser data collection on you) Step 2: Go to the settings and into the “My Filters” tab and add the following: www.youtube.com##div[class^='ytInlinePlayerControlsTopLeftControls'] www.youtube.com##.ytm-paid-content-overlay-renderer www.youtube.com##a[href*="https://support.google.com/youtube?p=ppp"] www.youtube.com##.ytp-paid-content-overlay

Work in progress ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ {.is-info}

Sailing The High Seas - Piracy and You

Yarrr! So it’s the pirate’s life for you, eh? Here’s information I’ve gleaned over the years…
Biggest thing is… If you like the software and you plan on using it a lot, purchase it to support the developers. (Unless it’s Adobe or Microsoft products)
This guide is purely for educational purposes. I will not provide tutorials on how to pirate specific software. Use your brain.

My personal notes for installing GPU drivers. AMD drivers were a lot simpler to install, but Nvidia drivers were their own kind of problem and docs didn’t always give reproducible results. It’s probably a me problem, but this saved me lots of problems with Nvidia drivers.

GPU Drivers

Prerequisites for installing on Virtual Machines (ESXI):

pciPassthru.use64bitMMIO = TRUE

pciPassthru.64bitMMIOSizeGB = 48

(Rule of thumb: MMIO size must be a power of 2 and at least twice the value of the current total VRAM for the VM. EX: V100 16gb = 32. M40 24GB = 48.)

Homebrew - https://brew.sh/

INSTALL COMMAND: /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

Homebrew is a free and open-source package manager that simplifies the installation of software on macOS and Linux.

UV - https://docs.astral.sh/uv/#installation

INSTALL COMMAND: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

UV is an extremely fast Python package and project manager written in Rust, designed to replace tools like pip and pip-tools.
